habitat: Small parties and flocks in thornveld, riverine bush, and exotic trees around homesteads and farms. Colonies are in trees away from water, including suburbia, or in waterside bushes and reeds. Nomadic when not breeding, often on farmland.
summary: A very common resident. The breeding male is yellow, with a black mask from the forehead to the throat, a pointed bib, a black bill and red eyes. The crown is more yellow than in Lesser Masked Weaver, and the back is plain. The female is greener above and whitish below, with a yellow wash on the breast. The non-breeding male resembles the female. The breeding female is slightly more yellow below and has redder eyes. The immature is duller, with greyer underparts. The call is a prolonged swizzling when breeding, plus a sharp zik. The Kemp paper name Masked Weaver and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Lesser Masked Weaver is smaller, with a rounded bib, a mask over the crown, pale yellow eyes and blue-grey legs. Southern Masked Weaver has red eyes and a pointed bib.

research.note: Newman calls it a very common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. It is nomadic when not breeding. No flight photograph was found. The grade A call is from Cape Town. Population figures and the Kemp name Masked Weaver were left unchanged.
